{{Orphan|date=June 2024}}

'''Kevin McConway''' (born 12 October 1950) is [[emeritus professor]] of [[applied statistics]] at the [[Open University]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/health-49877237 |title=Is red meat back on the menu? - BBC News |publisher=Bbc.co.uk |date=2019-09-30 |accessdate=2019-10-15}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.open.ac.uk/research/people/kjm2 |title=Professor Kevin McConway &#124; The Open University |publisher=Open.ac.uk |date= |accessdate=2019-10-15}}</ref> where he spent most of his career. He was the first Vice President (Academic Affairs) of the [[Royal Statistical Society]], from 2012-2016.

After growing up in Northumberland, McConway studied mathematics at [[Trinity College, Cambridge]] before taking a PhD at [[University College London|UCL]], under the supervision of [[Philip Dawid]].

He was academic adviser to the [[BBC Radio Four]] programme ''[[More or Less (radio programme)|More or Less]]''<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ciwf.org.uk/about-us/patrons-and-high-profile-supporters/visionaries/academia/kevin-mcconway/ |title=Kevin McConway &#124; Compassion in World Farming |publisher=[[Compassion in World Farming]] |date= |accessdate=2019-10-15 |archive-date=2019-10-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191001000615/https://www.ciwf.org.uk/about-us/patrons-and-high-profile-supporters/visionaries/academia/kevin-mcconway/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> and has written about that experience.<ref>{{cite journal|url=http://www.radstats.org.uk/no126/McConway126.pdf |journal=Radical Statistics|volume=126|year=2020|author=McConway, KJ|pages=20–26|title=BBC's More or Less and Covid-19}}</ref> He is currently a trustee and advisory board member of the [[Science Media Centre]] and has written about experience communicating statistics with the media,<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/abs/10.1177/1464884915593243 |title=Statistics and the Media: a statistician's view|journal=Journalism|volume=17|issue=1|pages=49–65|year=2016|author=McConway, KJ|doi=10.1177/1464884915593243|s2cid=141844133 |url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|volume = 9|issue = 5|pages = 45–48|year = 2012|journal = Significance|url = https://rss.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/j.1740-9713.2012.00611.x|doi = 10.1111/j.1740-9713.2012.00611.x|author1 = McConway, KJ|author2 = Spiegelhalter, DJ|title = Score and ignore: A radio listener's guide to ignoring health stories|url-access = subscription}}</ref> and this is developed as general guidance, and to statisticians specifically - "remember to sound human".<ref>{{cite journal|title=Sound human, steer clear of jargon, and be prepared|journal=Significance|volume=18|issue=2|pages=32–34|year=2021|author1=McConway, KJ|author2=[[Spiegelhalter]], DJ|doi=10.1111/1740-9713.01508|pmid=34230827 |pmc=8250941|doi-access=free}}</ref>

During the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], from November 2020 he was one of two [[Royal Statistical Society]] Fellows nominated to an advisory group to support the UK government prepare visualisations for broadcast press conferences.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://covid19.public-inquiry.uk/documents/inq000092893-witness-statement-of-cabinet-secretary-simon-case-dated-24-01-2023-and-provided-on-behalf-of-the-cabinet-office-corporate-statement/ | title=INQ000092893 - Witness statement of Cabinet Secretary Simon Case, dated 24/01/2023 and provided on behalf of the Cabinet Office (Corporate statement). UK Covid-19 Inquiry Archives }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://covid19.public-inquiry.uk/documents/inq000656298-witness-statement-of-robert-harrison-director-general-for-analysis-covid-19-taskforce-cabinet-office-dated-16-10-2025/ | title=IINQ000656298 – Witness statement of Robert Harrison, Director General for Analysis Covid-19 Taskforce, Cabinet Office, dated 16/10/2025}}</ref>
